items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Well, naturally George Morrow and I hung out -- bass players

ctx.x: However, so we were standing there by the band -- and they got up on the stand, and Leo said, "Why don't you let Wilbur sit in?" You know, he didn't tell me he wanted me, or that he was going to ask that, you know, so he said, "C'mon!" So he knew that Leo wouldn't say that if I couldn't play, so I asked George Morrow, and he said, "Uh huh, c'mon."

And so naturally, I don't know whether they had ever heard me, but you know, they liked to try you ... see, if you had the nerve to get up there and play, you had better be prepared to play. And right away, he called Cherokee, with the tempo very fast -- and oh, I felt so good, playing with these giants. And we went in to it. They were only playing for 30 minutes ... and we played 30 minutes.
